method: Models one bash parameter expansion at a time. The expansion is written as ${name...} and evaluated against the value typed into the page; the name is only a label, so ${file%.*} works with any value. Supported forms are the plain value, ${#name} for length, the default and alternative words ${name:-word}, ${name-word}, ${name:=word}, ${name=word}, ${name:+word}, ${name+word}, ${name:?word} and ${name?word}, the substrings ${name:offset} and ${name:offset:length}, prefix removal with ${name#pattern} and ${name##pattern}, suffix removal with ${name%pattern} and ${name%%pattern}, the substitutions ${name/pattern/repl} and ${name//pattern/repl}, and the case conversions ${name^}, ${name^^}, ${name,} and ${name,,}. The colon forms test for unset or empty and the bare forms test only for unset, exactly as bash does. Patterns use shell globbing: * matches any run of characters, ? matches one character, [abc] and [a-z] are character classes, [!abc] and [^abc] negate a class, and a backslash escapes the next character. A single # removes the shortest matching prefix and ## the longest, % removes the shortest matching suffix and %% the longest; substitution replaces the first match of the longest match at the earliest position, and // repeats that across the value, skipping empty matches the way bash does except for an empty value where a pattern that matches nothing at all still replaces once. Substring offsets are counted in characters: a negative offset counts back from the end, a value that starts past the end gives an empty string, a negative length is an end offset from the end, and bash's rejection of a negative length that ends before the offset is reproduced as an error. Length counts Unicode characters rather than bytes, and case conversion uses Unicode case mapping rather than the shell's locale. The page rejects command substitution, nested expansions, arrays, attribute operators, anchored substitutions and quoting instead of guessing at them, limits the expression to 400 characters, the value to 1000 characters and a pattern to 200 characters, and never runs a shell. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.
